answer: The defence rests on patent agent registration with filing record history: filings made for one practice across years. Forging 141 of these means building 141 separate filing records from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. Call it the forge rule: fakes pay per head, the honest pay once, the crystal record is open for audit, and the nebula window is too short for 141 aliases to earn their price back.
